records.text: A spectral undead apparition whose combat repertoire includes Scourge Strike.

Megelon is an injured survivor of the Exodar crash who puts others' survival ahead of personal injuries. Relieved when a fellow survivor awakens after weeks in suspension, Megelon trusts that survivor to help lead everyone to safety and passes on Proenitus's request to meet him. Megelon knows the crash killed many but does not explain its cause.
Jaeleil warmly welcomes heroes in Azure Watch and exchanges special gift vouchers for companion gifts. Jaeleil tells visitors that both are fortunate to be alive.

Proenitus coordinates care for the draenei survivors after their ship crashes in Ammen Vale. He urgently seeks to replenish depleted healing crystals, using vale moth blood as a substitute, while regretting that the creatures must die; he says indiscriminate killing is not the draenei way. His duties also include directing help to the wounded and scattered survivors.

A draenei crash survivor left exposed to irradiated crystals may be injured, frightened, or disoriented, and asks for help. Survivors remember the ship falling and evacuation pods; after receiving aid, they express gratitude and offer to help other survivors.

Keilnei is a hunter trainer who has long trained young draenei and intends to continue that work on the new world. She welcomes a promising hunter and offers to teach the class, presenting her service as a continuation of her responsibility to her people.

Valaatu is a mage trainer who has taught arcane, frost, and fire magic for more than a hundred years. He describes those powers as present on this world too, and presents magical practice as an endless path of discovery.

Aurelon is a paladin trainer who previously trained young paladins as they entered his order. He has taken up that duty again, calling it a privilege and offering to guide new paladins in their first steps in the Light.

Zalduun is a draenei priest tending the injured at the crash site. He asks visitors to use the Naaru’s gift to heal scattered survivors and needs vials to replenish the healing crystals. Even while caring for the wounded, he offers priestly guidance and trains those taking their first steps in the Light.
Kore is a draenei warrior trainer who has taught young warriors for centuries. He offers guidance to those beginning as warriors and sees potential in students who listen carefully to his teaching.

Botanist Taerix investigates the power crystal's effects on Ammen Vale's wildlife and develops a treatment for the lake. He asks for mutated lasher samples, sends help to disperse his neutralizing agent, and hopes to spare infected creatures from being killed. After the lake treatment, he tells his apprentice Tedon to test it on a captured beast.
A strange creature associated with the irradiated Exodar power cores near Ammen Vale. Botanist Taerix asks for their numbers to be culled while he considers a way to help them.
A mutated root lasher found in the irradiated Ammen Vale region.

Nestlewood owlkin encountered in the region around Ammen Vale. After inoculation, they show varied reactions, appearing overjoyed, disoriented, confused, appreciative, displeased, or seemingly unaffected by the crystal's effects.
Vale Moth is a small, low-level creature found across several areas of Ammen Vale. Its records show no conversational or service role.
Blood Elf Scouts patrol the Shadow Ridge area as part of the blood-elf threat in Ammen Vale. They confront intruders with threats and warn that they will not let survivors leave the valley.

Surveyor Candress is a blood-elf leader whose presence directs the scouting party in Ammen Vale. The crash-site defenders see her removal as a way to disrupt the party and gain time while repairs are completed; when confronted, she declares she will not be taken alive.

Vindicator Aldar helps coordinate the crash-site survivors' response to problems around Ammen Vale, including missing scouts, the blood-elf scouting party, and the effort to inoculate affected owlkin. After hearing that blood elves are present, he says he will send someone to retrieve Tolaan. He also offers the newcomer guidance about choosing a path of the Light.

Mutated Owlkin are among the creatures changed by contamination from the wreckage in Silverline Lake. The mutation has made many nearby creatures hostile, and the owlkin are treated as a danger in Nestlewood Thicket.

Tolaan is a scout who was ambushed by blood elves on Shadow Ridge and barely managed to call for help. Though badly hurt, he reports that the blood elves threaten the survivors and urges them to weaken the attackers so the others have a chance.
Technician Dyvuun is trying to repair a signal emitter and establish clear contact with Zhanna.

Caregiver Chellan is Azure Watch's innkeeper, offering travelers a place to stay and goods to buy. She receives Aeun's report about the stranded survivors and says someone will be sent to tend Aeun's injured leg.

Aeun is an Azure Watch scout injured by mutated beasts while on a mission. Unable to travel with her injured leg, she asks a passing traveler to carry her report to Caregiver Chellan; she also longs for a healing crystal.

Shalannius is a druid trainer who offers guidance to those seeking to develop as druids. He urges people to help heal the land ravaged by the crash, while recognizing that they may not share his philosophy. He also provides options for talent resets and dual talent specialization.
Aurok is an armorsmith who sells goods to visitors. The available evidence establishes his trade and shop role, without further personal details.
Jel is a cloth and leather merchant who sells goods to visitors. The available evidence identifies the kinds of goods associated with Jel’s trade, without further personal details.
Mura is a weaponsmith who sells goods to visitors. The available evidence establishes her trade and shop role; a quest mentioning another Mura does not establish that it concerns this weaponsmith.
Ryosh is a general supplies merchant who sells goods to visitors. The available evidence identifies his shop role, without further personal details.
An Ammen Vale guardian, stationed in the draenei settlement on Azuremyst Isle.
An injured Draenei humanoid on Azuremyst Isle.

Technician Zhanaa works to repair a salvaged holographic emitter so it can help find survivors beyond Ammen Vale. She seeks spare parts, then urges the player to ask Azure Watch for aid and supplies for the crash survivors. Her excitement when the emitter works reflects how much the discovery means to the stranded group.
The Draenei Mourner grieves for Luhanaa, calling her their love and asking that she rest in peace. They blame the crash for her death and bitterly wish to find those responsible.

The Spirit of the Vale teaches that earth gives strength and steadiness, while the elements must remain in balance. The Spirit is wary of the draenei’s arrival, which angered the earth spirits, but recognizes a shaman’s bravery and shares its wisdom. It urges shaman to use elemental power with care and preserve that balance.

Firmanvaar is a draenei shaman trainer who guides those beginning to relearn shamanism among the draenei. He teaches respect for the elements and helps students form a bond with earth through their totem. He hopes restoring balance between the earth element and the draenei will build understanding among those who disapprove of shamanism. He describes continuing Farseer Nobundo’s shamanistic teachings as a duty and honor.

Diktynna is the fishing trainer and supply keeper at Azure Watch’s river. A murloc attack injured her while she was netting red snapper, leaving her unable to fish; she asks for help securing food for the draenei. She is grateful for the catch and offers to teach fishing. Her concern about murlocs and lasting memory of sharing the snapper reflect the danger and relief behind the task.

Acteon trains hunters at Azure Watch and directs local work. He sends hunters after moongraze stags and the more formidable bucks, treating the hunt as a progression in skill; he also points aspiring hunters toward Dazalar for the path to a pet. Concerned by Diktynna’s injury, he hopes she recovers and offers work. He jokes about hunters being sent away for burial, then clarifies they were sent to the Exodar for treatment of minor wounds. He made his own comfortable armor, distinct from traditional draenei wear.

Arugoo of the Stillpine tells of Akida’s prophecy: a hero from outside the furbolg people will help save the Stillpine from Bristlelimb. He asks the foretold hero to free Stillpine captives, then directs them to High Chief Stillpine at Stillpine Hold for the next challenge.

Exarch Menelaous takes responsibility for the harm caused by ignored reports of crystal debris in the river and urges action to stop the resulting contamination. He speaks of the draenei’s long flight from the Burning Legion as ending on Azuremyst, where they will stand and fight. When he learns a spy has watched their work, he resolves to alert Prophet Velen and await his direction.

An injured night elf priestess, she groans and sits up, then cries out to Elune in confusion. Seeing eredar, she believes she has been brought there with companions and declares they will fight the demons as they have before.

A restless earth spirit in Ammen Vale, caught in the disturbance surrounding the draenei crash. The elementals of the Vale are at odds: the earth spirits have turned against the other elements, and restoring balance means confronting them.
An air spirit of Azuremyst Isle.
A water spirit of Ammen Vale, one of the elemental presences gathered where the draenei crash unsettled the Vale. Its kind is among the elements caught in the resulting discord.
A fire spirit of Ammen Vale, one of the elemental presences gathered where the draenei crash unsettled the Vale. Its kind is among the elements caught in the resulting discord.
A Bristlelimb furbolg of Azuremyst Isle, among the furbolgs found across the surrounding Vale and nearby terrain.
A Bristlelimb furbolg known as a windcaller, found among the Bristlelimb people of Azuremyst Isle. In combat, this windcaller uses Wind Shock.
A Bristlelimb Ursa of Azuremyst Isle.
A Deranged Owlbeast is a beast of Azuremyst Isle. Its native record identifies no named service or story role.
An Aberrant Owlbeast is a beast of Azuremyst Isle. Its combat record includes Moonfire, but gives it no named service or story role.
A Raving Owlbeast is a beast whose native behavior includes a frenzy display and enrage in combat. The supplied records do not connect it to a ritual or other story role.
Crazed Wildkin are among the attackers inside Stillpine Hold. Stillpine the Younger asks the player to slay them alongside their leader, Chieftain Oomooroo.
Siltfin Murlocs are recorded across several Azuremyst Isle areas. The supplied native data gives them no named service or story role.
Siltfin Oracles are recorded across several Azuremyst Isle areas. Their native record includes a combat behavior that disables combat movement; it gives no named service or story role.

A Siltfin Hunter is one of the hostile hunters found around Azuremyst Isle’s western naga-occupied ruins and nearby areas. It is a ranged fighter that throws weapons at a distance, switches to melee up close, and may flee for help when badly wounded.

Wrathscale Naga are among the naga occupying the ruined night elf city west of Odesyus’ Landing, according to Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare. This hostile naga combatant in the surrounding ruins uses Hamstring.

A Wrathscale Myrmidon is one of the naga occupying the ruined night elf city west of Odesyus’ Landing, as Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare describes them. It is a hostile combatant found among those ruins and uses Strike.

Wrathscale Sirens are part of the naga force occupying the ruined night elf city west of Odesyus’ Landing, according to Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare. This hostile creature is found in the ruins and uses Screech in combat.
Root Trapper is the name of a creature found across several areas of Azuremyst Isle, including parts of the western ruins.
Root Thresher is the name of a creature found in several areas of Azuremyst Isle, including the western ruins.
Ravager specimen: a close-range attacker that tears at nearby foes with Rend and Ravage.
A Moongraze stag, a wild creature found in the Azuremyst region.
A Moongraze buck, a wild creature that knocks down its foes in combat.
An infected nightstalker runt, one of the animals targeted for cleanup after Exodar crystal fragments were found in the river. Exarch Menelaous warns that the infection could spread.
A nightstalker, one of the big cats of Azuremyst. Huntress Kella describes nightstalkers as efficient, deadly hunters that can become allies when tamed.

Temper is a powerful fire elemental at Emberglade, sent there by Tuluun to help a shaman understand fire. He sees flame as both destructive and renewing: it should consume what it burns, then die and be reborn. He opposes his deranged brother Hauteur’s claim to godhood among the owlbeasts and teaches that ending Hauteur’s suffering restores balance. Temper describes the shaman’s actions as destroying and saving Hauteur, whose ashes mark his promised rebirth.

Tuluun is a Broken draenei shaman at Azure Watch who trains shamans in the ways of the spirits and guides their understanding of elemental fire. He sends a promising student to Temper at Emberglade as part of the fire totem trial, then receives the student after the encounter with Hauteur. Tuluun connects that trial’s destruction and renewal to the tribulation of the draenei people. He acknowledges that Broken and draenei may face ridicule, and says understanding and communicating with the elements matters most.

Anchorite Fateema teaches first aid at Azure Watch, stressing that proper bandaging can decide life or death. She has developed a healing ointment from root trapper vines, but the many injured draenei leave supplies scarce. She fears for an unconscious guest found near the Crystalbrook and hopes the ointment will help, later expressing disappointment at its ineffectiveness. Fateema insists her people are not eredar and urges explaining this to the guest and others like her.

Daedal teaches alchemy at Azure Watch and urgently seeks an alternative treatment for an injured guest when ointments are insufficient. He turns to azure snapdragon, a plant reputed to cure all ailments, and reassures the guest that she is safe. Her reaction to his people leads him to reconsider Velen's prophecy about allies demanding payment for ancestral sins; he sends an envoy to find her kin and explain his people's history.
Hauteur Reborn is a reborn being who speaks with a shaman after looking toward Temper. Grateful for the help, Hauteur sees this renewal as a chance to burn brighter than before.

Artificer Daelo is an engineering trainer sent from the Exodar to oversee Azure Watch's construction. He also offers engineering wares, serving the settlement as both a technical instructor and a supplier.
This draenei artificer is openly hostile toward Tuluun, whom they accuse of spreading heresy. They resent Tuluun's presence, reject the shaman's kind, and turn back to work with disgust.

Cryptographer Aurren studies the symbols carved on Stillpine furbolg totems, hoping to understand their language. He has worked out a rudimentary symbol matrix and gives the player a primer to help interpret the totems and learn to communicate with the furbolgs.

Admiral Odesyus commands the stranded Alliance naval expedition at Odesyus' Landing. After goblins steal the ships' navigation gear, a recovered map reveals plans to exploit the island and hijack the ships; Odesyus suspects a traitor among his crew and recruits outside help to investigate. He is wary of trust, but his banter with Cookie shows a dry, teasing side.

Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare is a night elf who sees the naga threat as an assault on her people's ancestral lands. She believes fate brought her people to Azuremyst Isle and asks for help driving the naga from the ruined city to the west. Though grateful to her allies, she remains wary of draenei, whose resemblance to the eredar troubles her; she says their aid may gradually ease her doubts and fears.

Archaeologist Adamant Ironheart is a dwarf of the Explorers' League who retired from Ironforge's elite guard, where he says he served as King Magni's right hand. He now pursues archaeology as a hobby and a way to travel. On Azuremyst Isle he seeks night elf relics, crediting his interest to his father's advice, and deciphers a tablet that warns of Warlord Sriss'tiz's invasion plans and reinforcements from Nazjatar.

Engineer “Spark” Overgrind is a gnome spy posing as an envoy of Mekkatorque. He betrayed the Alliance and works for Kael’thas, guarding information about the Exodar and coordinating with Geezle. He threatens Geezle over failure and speaks openly of serving the Legion. His cover is exposed in the plot surrounding the meeting at the cove.
An Alliance axeman in Azuremyst Isle.
Blacksmith Calypso is an island blacksmith who trains blacksmithing and offers supplies. She may say she knew Spark for years and was surprised to learn he was a traitor.

Cookie McWeaksauce is a reformed pirate cook at the expedition, proud of his family’s cooking trade and practicing his pirate speech. He trains cooks and sells supplies; worried that another chicken dinner will frustrate the crew, he asks for crawler meat to make gumbo and lift morale.
An Alliance logger.
An image of Technician Zhanaa reaches out to Dyvuun, but the transmission is badly broken. She can barely hear him and seems to be waking as static interrupts her words.
A flaming aspect, a fire elemental.
Temper’s Target is a target associated with Temper.
A Venture Co. saboteur, identified by the company affiliation and destructive trade in its name. It attacks intruders with thorn magic.
The Venture Co. Gemologist is identified by a gemologist's trade and a Venture Co. association.
Ragnarose is Cookie's parrot, an animal companion identified through its association with Cookie.

Warlord Sriss'tiz is a warlord whose reign Priestess Kyleen Il'dinare wants to end, fearing a naga invasion. Kyleen only suspects he may be hiding in a cave west along the coast; she does not know his whereabouts.

Magwin fears her parents were slain after murlocs and owlkin attacked her family, yet sets out through the forest to reach home. During the reunion, she exclaims with relief on finding her father alive, mourns the ruined house and thanks her escort.
A carved furbolg totem whose markings offer a clue in the language exercise. Its primal images include owls, bears, wolves and stags; the symbols resolve into “Coo.”
A carved furbolg totem whose markings offer a clue in the language exercise. Its primal images include owls, bears, wolves and stags; the symbols resolve into “Tikti.”
A carved furbolg totem whose markings offer a clue in the language exercise. Its symbols resolve into “Yor,” and its directions identify Bristlelimb Village to the west.
A carved furbolg totem bearing images of conflict between the Stillpine and Bristlelimb tribes. Its inscription gives the word “Vark,” meaning justice.
A young timberstrider, one of the wildlife found around Azuremyst Isle.
Timberstriders are beasts of Azuremyst Isle. The taming lesson uses them to teach hunters to befriend a more powerful animal.
Greater Timberstriders are powerful beasts found in northern Azuremyst Isle. They are used in a hunter's lesson in taming a more capable animal.
A captive of the Stillpine, held in Bristlelimb Village. When freed, the captive speaks of the prophecy and promises that those remaining at Stillpine Hold will welcome the rescuer as a hero.
A vale hunter encountered in Azuremyst Isle's vale.

Velaada is one of Farseer Nobundo's accomplished pupils, studying the element of air at Wildwind Peak. She welcomes visitors and teaches the air lesson before directing the student to Susurrus for deeper understanding.
A Stillpine Defender is a humanoid defender associated by name with the Stillpine people. Defenders are present in the Azuremyst area.

Susurrus is an air spirit at Wildwind Peak who teaches a lesson about the element of air to a shaman seeking wisdom. He recognizes the visitor's prior effort and gives them a Whorl of Air to take to Farseer Nobundo for help fashioning a totem. When the visitor chooses the offered option, Susurrus can fly them down to the Exodar.
Called Aspect of Air, this elemental is found around Wildwind Peak.
A Stillpine Defender corpse in the Azuremyst area associated with the Stillpine people.
A Crazed Wildkin corpse in the Azuremyst area associated with the Stillpine people.
A Stillpine Hunter is a humanoid hunter associated by name with the Stillpine people and found in the Azuremyst area.

High Chief Stillpine leads the Stillpine furbolgs through a crisis that has turned former allies against them. He seeks the cause of the corruption in Stillpine Hold and investigates blood-red crystals dissolving into the cave’s water. Guided by the prophecy of the Promised One, he weighs the tribe’s peril against its future and speaks of the danger and unanswered visions facing others as well.

Gurf is a Stillpine provisioner and skinning trainer with a proud streak and a very personal grievance against the Siltfin murlocs. Their attack on the tribe’s food stores leaves him concerned for its grain, while his account of a murloc kicking him and the recovery of his missing fur turn the dispute into an indignity he treats with comic seriousness. He calls himself Gurf the Brave.

Moordo is Stillpine’s elder hunter and a leatherworker who turns the hides of ravagers and the Kurken into armor. He reads the strange beasts as signs of an approaching apocalypse and sees the listener as the Promised One destined to stop it. His manner mixes solemn prophecy with dry humor.

Kurz interprets his visions as a prophecy about the Kurken and believes the listener is the one destined to defeat it, Stillpine’s only hope. He asks for the beast’s hide as proof, then hails the listener as the Promised One when the task is reported complete. His certainty makes him a fervent, self-assured village revelator.
Magtor the Blind Watcher is a humanoid on Azuremyst Isle.

Stillpine the Younger identifies himself as heir to the Stillpine throne and legacy. From his position at Stillpine Hold, he rallies the raiders against the wildkin attacking the hold and calls for a strike after Chieftain Oomooroo is slain. His words frame the fight as a chance for the Stillpine to push back and protect their home.
Parkat Steelfur is a general goods vendor at Stillpine Hold. He welcomes customers to his shop; his name is distinct from the other Stillpine figures.
Chieftain Oomooroo leads the crazed wildkin in Stillpine Hold. Stillpine the Younger sees Oomooroo as the obstacle preventing the defenders from striking inside the hold.

Ruada trains warriors at Azure Watch and describes her own teacher, Behomat, as a wiser hand to whom she now entrusts her student. For one trial, she gives the trainee a key to release a caged death ravager and asks that it be killed with a simple blade, since it is lightly armored but resists most magic. She frames the task as preventing further damage to the isle's ecology. After the beast is defeated, Ruada solemnly says the trainee is ready for the next lesson and directs them to Behomat.

Semid is a mage trainer at Azure Watch. He describes arcane and elemental practice as an unending path of discovery, and warns that unchecked magic can corrupt souls and destroy worlds. His counsel frames control as essential to a mage’s training.

Guvan is a priest trainer at Azure Watch and a devout follower of the Light. Concerned when the herbalist Tavara has been gone too long, she asks a fellow priest to find and heal her, explaining that she cannot search herself. She regards the Light as a source of guidance and blessing.

Tullas is a paladin trainer at Azure Watch who describes the path of the Light as one of purity and righteousness, while acknowledging that even he sometimes struggles to follow it. He directs a promising student to his former teacher, Jol, whose instruction began his own journey.

Buruk is a pet trainer at Azure Watch, offering hunters guidance in training their pets and the option to untrain them. His greeting frames the service as training a hunter can pass on to their companion.
Esbina is a stable master at Azure Watch. She offers to stable pets and help recover lost companions, presenting her role as practical support for travelers and their animal companions.
Ziz is a tradesman at Windshear Crag. He sells goods there; Piznik’s account identifies him as the former boss at the mining site, but does not establish Ziz’s current plans or whereabouts.
Erin Kelly is a tailoring trainer. Her exchange offers tailoring instruction, establishing her role as a practical guide for aspiring tailors in the Azure Watch area.
Dulvi teaches mining at Azure Watch. After hearing an injured guest speak in fevered dreams of Cowlen’s distress at Silvermyst Isle, Dulvi voices concern and asks for help finding him.
Logan Daniel is a general-goods vendor in Azure Watch, with ammunition among the goods associated with his shop.
Ergh of the Stillpine trades supplies in Azure Watch. Ergh greets a visitor and offers access to their wares, marking a distinct Stillpine presence among the area’s traders.

A Stillpine raider encountered in Azuremyst Isle, this combatant attacks at close range with Heroic Strike. The available records establish its role in combat but offer no further personal history or conversational identity.
Tavara is an herbalist who left Azure Watch to search for herbs near the hot springs. Guvan fears she may be hurt.

This Draenei youngling hunts infected nightstalkers and boasts that the task should be easy, but calls for help when a beast becomes too much to handle. Their pleas and fear of being overwhelmed show the danger behind that confidence. After surviving the encounter, they thank their rescuer and ask that Exarch Menelaous hear what happened.

Blood Elf bandits threaten their victims for money and then promise death if resisted. Their cries invoke Silvermoon, Sunstrider, and a tribute to the King, giving their violence a clear political allegiance; in combat they use Heroic Strike.

A Quel'dorei magewraith consumed by magic, used as a warning of the destruction unchecked magic can bring. Displays of spellcasting at the Silting Shore attract its attention, and it challenges anyone daring to wield magic in its presence.

Huntress Kella Nightbow guides novice hunters beyond killing toward bonds with animals, using Stillpine-carved totems for temporary taming lessons. She demands increasing tenacity as pupils progress from barbed crawlers to greater timberstriders, teasing them about claws and the danger of pecked eyes. Thundris Windweaver is an old friend whom she recommends as a respected recipient of an introduction in Auberdine.
Kioni sells cloth and leather.
Nabek is a weapons and armor merchant who also repairs equipment. Visitors can browse his goods.
Heur is an herbalism trainer who offers instruction in the profession.
Azuremyst Peacekeepers offer visitors assistance around the isle. Their recorded directions cover the bank and the hippogryph master.

Otonambusi is a general-goods vendor who also offers ammunition. His brief spoken lines repeat a comic fish-and-pudding refrain: if you do not eat your fish, you cannot have pudding. That playful warning gives this practical shopkeeper a distinctive bit of flavor.

Apprentice Tedon helps address the crystal's effects on the lake near the Crash Site. He opens a cage, applies a neutralizing agent, and celebrates when the attempt succeeds. He also believes Botanist Taerix may be close to a breakthrough.

Apprentice Vishael studies the corruption affecting the Ammen Fields and their lashers. Vishael asks for corrupted flowers to examine, hoping the specimens will help determine how the fields might be restored, and trusts Botanist Taerix to find solutions to their problems.
A Stormwind marine serving the Alliance, trained for close combat. The marine blocks attacks with a shield and answers with a shield strike.
Crusty Bob is a beast in the local area.

The Azuremyst Isle Flame Warden welcomes people to honor the local flame and urges honoring Alliance settlement fires. Its festival message calls Horde fires unworthy and encourages their desecration.
A weapons vendor who also repairs equipment, offering visitors both arms and maintenance. Their work is practical and direct: they keep weapons available and help adventurers restore damaged gear.

The Cheerful Draenei Spirit in the Exodar’s graveyard enjoys visiting friends and family again, celebrating and sharing old stories. Having eaten everything prepared for the visit, the spirit politely asks for more Bread of the Dead and gratefully offers a small holiday gift in return.
A Ghostly Draenei Celebrant enjoys visiting friends and family again, celebrating and sharing old stories.

place_records.text: You are in Azuremyst Isle, Alliance land on the continent of Kalimdor. Its settlements are Azure Watch, Odesyus' Landing, Wildwind Peak and the Crash Site, where the draenei ship came down, and the Alliance keeps them all. Murlocs haunt the waters, nightstalkers roam the woods, and blood elf bandits are a menace in the wilds.

You are in Ammen Vale, a valley around the draenei crash site on Azuremyst Isle. Survivors of the Exodar crash gather here, and wounded draenei ask for help. Blood elf scouts guard Shadow Ridge and threaten survivors who try to leave the valley. A spirit healer can return the dead to life for a price.

You are in the Crash Site, the draenei camp in the wreckage of the ship, where survivors of Ammen Vale gather. Proenitus coordinates their care, and Zalduun tends the wounded in the central chamber. Draenei trainers teach magic, arms and faith here, and a vendor and repairs are available. Vindicator Aldar helps direct the response to the blood elf scouting party.

You are in Silverline Lake, a lake in Ammen Vale fouled by contamination from the crash wreckage. Botanist Taerix is working on a treatment for the lake and sends help to spread his neutralizing agent.

You are in Nestlewood Thicket, a wooded stretch of Ammen Vale where owlkin live. Some owlkin have been inoculated against the crystal's effects and act strangely, while mutated owlkin have turned hostile and are a danger here.

You are in Shadow Ridge, a ridge in Ammen Vale patrolled by blood elf scouts. Surveyor Candress directs the scouting party here. The scouts threaten intruders and vow that survivors will not leave the valley.

You are in Ammen Fields, a part of Ammen Vale where irradiated land has mutated the plants and creatures. Mutated root lashers and volatile mutations live here, and Botanist Taerix wants the volatile ones culled while he seeks a way to help them. Draenei survivors exposed to the crystals wander here and ask for help.

You are in The Sacred Grove, a grove in Ammen Vale where the Spirit of the Vale speaks of earth's steadiness. The spirit is wary of the draenei, whose arrival angered the earth spirits. Restless spirits of earth are a danger in the grove.

You are in Emberglade, a glade on Azuremyst Isle where fire elementals gather. Temper, a powerful fire elemental, opposes his deranged brother Hauteur, who has been reborn and wants to burn brighter than before.
You are in Moonwing Den, a den of owlbeasts on Azuremyst Isle. Deranged, raving and aberrant owlbeasts make the den dangerous.
You are in Pod Cluster on Azuremyst Isle. Moongraze bucks and root trappers live here, while infected nightstalker runts and blood elf bandits make the area dangerous.
You are in Pod Wreckage on Azuremyst Isle. Wild Moongraze stags and root trappers live here, and blood elf bandits are a danger.

You are in Wrathscale Point, a bare stretch of Azuremyst Isle with no settlements. Wrathscale nagas, sirens and myrmidons are the danger here, and root trappers and moongraze stags are the only other creatures about.

You are in Bristlelimb Village, a furbolg settlement on Azuremyst Isle that is home to the Bristlelimb tribe. Bristlelimb windcallers, ursas and furbolgs are hostile, and blood elf bandits are about too. Stillpine captives are caged here, and a carved totem recounts the war between the two tribes.

You are in Stillpine Hold, a furbolg stronghold on Azuremyst Isle kept by the Stillpine tribe, which sides with the Alliance. High Chief Stillpine leads his people through a crisis of corrupted wildkin, and Moordo and Gurf teach crafts here. Siltfin murlocs have raided the food stores, and a beast called the Kurken is feared.

You are in Odesyus' Landing, the camp of a stranded Alliance naval expedition on Azuremyst Isle, under Admiral Odesyus. Engineer Spark Overgrind, a gnome spy who betrayed the Alliance and works for Kael'thas, is among those here. Goblins stole the ships' navigation gear and fled into the thicket to the east, and the camp offers a cook, a smith, a tailor and goods traders.

You are in Silting Shore, a stretch of Azuremyst Isle where Siltfin murlocs hunt along the water. Siltfin murlocs, oracles and hunters are the main threat, with root threshers, a murgurgula and a Quel'dorei magewraith also about.

You are in Azure Watch, a draenei settlement on Azuremyst Isle held by the Alliance. It has an inn, a stable, repairs, and trainers in arms, magic, healing and crafts. Many injured draenei are here and supplies are scarce, the healer Fateema warns, while Acteon sends hunters after moongraze stags.

You are in Geezle's Camp, a goblin camp on Azuremyst Isle under the goblin leader Geezle, who plots with a traitor in the Alliance ranks. Venture Company saboteurs and gemologists are the danger here, and timberstrider fledglings wander about.
You are in Menagerie Wreckage, a wreck on Azuremyst Isle. Ravager specimens are the main danger here in great numbers, and blood elf bandits also prowl the wreck.

You are in Wildwind Peak, a settlement on a mountain peak of Azuremyst Isle, held by the Alliance. Shamans come here to learn the elements, from air taught by Velaada to the air spirit Susurrus. It also has an inn, a bank, a battlemaster, and trainers in many crafts and arts.

You are in Wildwind Path, the route up the north face of the mountain the Exodar crashed into on Azuremyst Isle. Shaman trainers Farseer Nobundo and Sulaa teach here, and Dekin sells fishing supplies.
You are in Silvermyst Isle, an island where owlbeasts hunt. Aberrant, raving and deranged owlbeasts are the danger here, and a Quel'dorei magewraith also haunts the isle.

You are in Ammen Ford, a river crossing on Azuremyst Isle where draenei fish for red snapper. Diktynna gives fishing instruction and keeps supplies, but a murloc attack injured her while she was netting and she can no longer fish.

You are in Moongraze Woods, a wooded part of Azuremyst Isle in Kalimdor, on Alliance land. Wild Moongraze stags and bucks roam the trees, and a carved furbolg totem stands here with markings that read as Coo. Tavara, an herbalist who left Azure Watch, has gone searching for herbs near the hot springs. Infected nightstalker runts and timberstriders prowl the woods.
